newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to speed up bomb shelter programme.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to speed up bomb shelter programme.

text.p: Singapore is to speed up its programme to provide access to bomb shelters for all its citizens by passing a law requiring all new housing developments to include such shelters.

Home Affairs (Interior) Minister Wong Kan Seng said in a speech on Monday night that bomb shelters had been provided in some underground railway stations, government-built apartment blocks and schools.
"Up to now, the government has built all shelters," he said. "We intend to pass legislation next year to require shelters to be built in all new housing developments."

He did not say which potential enemy the government thought might make bomb shelters necessary. But he likened the programme to those in Switzerland and Sweden and indicated it would be many years before there were enough to protect Singapore's population of nearly three million.
"It will take a long time to reach this goal. Switzerland and Sweden began several decades ago, but their shelter-building programmes are still incomplete," he said.
